# Auth

- A custom guard extends `BaseGuard`, not only `Guard`: `AuthInterceptor` attaches the auth header and handles a 401 only when `Auth.guard() is BaseGuard`, so a bare `Guard` sends every request unauthenticated.
- `AuthManager` caches each guard by name and passes `setUserFactory`'s factory to a guard when it builds it. A factory set after the first `Auth.guard()` never reaches the cached guard, and `loadCachedUser` then returns null. Call `forgetGuards()` after a late `setUserFactory` or `extend`, during setup only: it drops each cached guard with its in-memory user and token, the next `Auth.guard()` builds a guest-state guard, and the session returns only through `restore()` (at boot) or a sign-in. The boot-order rule for `setUserFactory` is in `CLAUDE.md`.
- With a `BaseGuard` active, `AuthInterceptor.onError` acts on a 401 only when the refused request carried the guard's current credential; with any other `Guard` every 401 on a request that carried a credential goes to refresh, a failed refresh calls `Auth.logout()`, and nothing is replayed. Under a `BaseGuard`, a request sent before sign-in or with an older token is handed back refused, not replayed. A refresh belongs to the session it started in (`BaseGuard.sessionEpoch`, `@internal`): when a sign-in or a sign-out lands meanwhile, the refreshed token is discarded and the refused request is handed back without a retry or a logout, and a retry already on its way keeps the refreshed token (`_pinnedCredential`) instead of picking up the new session's.
- A sign-in (`startSession`, and `storeToken`, which counts as one) is a new session: it deletes the stored refresh token before it writes its access token and writes its own refresh token last. `Vault` operations finish in the order they were issued (`MagicVaultService._run`), and `restore()` stops when a sign-in or a sign-out begins during its reads.
- The token, the refresh token and the cached user payload go through `Vault` only (`base_guard.dart`). Do not write them to `Storage` or `Cache`: secure storage is the one place a credential may sit.
